# Arterial Intelligence

> Arterial Intelligence is a vascular diagnostics company developing a noninvasive, point-of-care Doppler platform designed to support vascular assessment for peripheral artery disease (PAD). It works independent of pressure ratios and cuff occlusion. The platform is an investigational device: it has not been cleared or approved by the U.S. FDA and is not available for sale in the United States.

## The problem

- 21M+ U.S. adults are estimated to have peripheral artery disease (PAD).
- 1/3 of PAD patients have arteries too stiff to compress, causing current tests to fail.
- 30% of PAD patients are dead within 5 years because their disease is caught too late.
- The ankle-brachial index (ABI) is fast and cheap, but in patients with calcified, noncompressible arteries (common in diabetes and chronic kidney disease) it can be unreliable or inconclusive.

## The approach

- As disease narrows an artery, the Doppler waveform downstream changes in a recognizable way, and calcification doesn't distort it the way it distorts cuff pressure. Arterial Intelligence is built around that signal.
- Three steps in one visit: Scan (a handheld probe captures arterial waveforms in minutes at the point of care), Analyze (software-supported waveform interpretation intended to aid clinical assessment), Act (structured output designed to fit the clinical workflow and help prepare guideline-directed next steps).
- Designed for primary care, podiatry, wound clinics and health systems.

## Team

- Josh Hanson, Chief Executive Officer: Biodesign trained; Mayo Clinic Gonda Vascular Center.
- Alex Richardson, Chief Technology Officer: engineer for DARPA, Medtronic and Abbott; $100M raised and 3 medtech exits.
- Chris Galando, Head of Commercialization: 20+ years in sales leadership; led cardiovascular sales for Johnson & Johnson and Stryker.
- Robert McBane, MD, Chair of the Scientific Advisory Board: 25+ years in cardiovascular medicine at Mayo Clinic; 200+ publications; Master of the Society for Vascular Medicine.
